The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Picture That Wouldn’t Stay

Caty found a silver curl on a dock leaf. Beside it was a dot and beside the dot a smaller curl. Slug was sliding away from the last one. “Did you draw that?” she asked. “With my whole tummy,” said Slug.

Everybody Day needed pictures. Caty asked if she could hang a frame around this one. Slug said she could try. Caty fetched a frame of twigs. By the time she came back, the silver curl was awfully hard to see.

She tilted the leaf toward the sun. Nothing. She tilted it toward the hedge. There! Then a drop slid down the middle and changed the little dot into a comma. The picture kept doing things.

“I could copy it on paper,” Caty offered. Slug thought about it. “Could you copy the bit where it disappears?” Caty tried drawing an invisible curl. Her paper looked remarkably like paper.

So she asked a different question. “Would you make a picture while people watch?” Slug stretched out until he was very long. “I should like that. Will they have a little while? My tummy works slowly.”

They tried a show for Bella. Slug drew half a curl. Bella leaned to one side to find it. He drew the other half. Bella leaned the other way. Caty watched the watcher. That was a sort of dance.

On her leaf for the Welcome Tree, Caty drew a spiral and one dewdrop. “A picture of where to look,” she told Slug. “The picture itself will be whatever your tummy feels like that day.”

Slug’s next picture took all morning. Caty brought her breakfast and stayed. Just before the sun moved, a great silvery S appeared. “Is that for Slug?” she asked. “Could be,” he said. “Could be for supper.”

Read together

How could you share a picture that changes as you watch?
